searchText: <@!273808422753796097> the latest that Alex and me have proposed is here: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-2926 we're trying to fill in the constants (create gas overhead, etc.) now Hmm, why are you using the full binary trie spec here? Surely it's overkill for something where keys are inherently sequential and a simple binary tree suffices? hmm ok so this is not trying to fit it inside SSZ, it's using various direct byte concatenation tricks I have a local branch for a variant with SSZ and would be happy to propose that one too. The reason the default variant uses the binary spec and simple byte concat is to reduce complexity by avoiding to introduce a merkleization and serialization rule My instinct would definitely be to favor the SSZ one simply because that moves toward reducing long-run *total* complexity of ethereum I can fully understand that. I'll bring up both variants on ACD next time code merkleization is discussed to see what client devs think

excerpts.content: Hmm, why are you using the full binary trie spec here? Surely it's overkill for something where keys are inherently sequential and a simple binary tree suffices?

excerpts.content: hmm ok so this is not trying to fit it inside SSZ, it's using various direct byte concatenation tricks

excerpts.content: I have a local branch for a variant with SSZ and would be happy to propose that one too. The reason the default variant uses the binary spec and simple byte concat is to reduce complexity by avoiding to introduce a merkleization and serialization rule
